messages:
sara: Heads-up, spotted a p99 regression in staging for short-seq requests after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. Seeing ~20% increase on token-level tail for routes that have high KV cache hit rates. :frowning:

mike: ugh. which heuristic change?

sara: the change made the selector prefer the 'packed_matmul_v2' kernel whenever avg_batch_size > 1.2 to optimize throughput. that was fine for long sequences, but for seq_len <= 32 and with KV cache hits (so very short remaining tokens) packed_matmul_v2 is slower on GPU because it adds a memcpy step.

raj: do we have profiling traces? flamegraph or timeline?

sara: yes — attached perf snippets in the staging run: 
```
-- kernel: packed_matmul_v2
-- avg_batch: 1.35
-- seq_len: 24
-- kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.82
gpu_kernel_ns: 4200
cpu_overhead_ns: 200
expected_opt_ns: 3300
```

elaine: interesting. so higher KV hits correlate with smaller active token work, making memcpy dominating. can we correlate kernel_choice vs kv_hit vs p99?

oliver: i ran a quick query in prometheus: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
```
and overlaid kernel_choice label from our selector logs. when kernel_choice=="packed_matmul_v2" and seq_len_bucket=="<=32" p99 goes up ~18-22% on route /chat/light.

sara: yep. also saw batch_size_histograms shift — median batch size is ~1, but selector flip makes us pick packed kernel for the occasional 2nd request in a microbatch and that path costs us for everyone due to tail amplification.

mike: short-term mitigation: revert that heuristic? or add a seq_len threshold when kv_hit_ratio > 0.6?

raj: before rolling back, can we improve observability so this doesn't surprise us again. proposal: add kernel_choice as a metric label and expose kernel_choice counters in runtime with labels: model, route, seq_len_bucket, kv_cache_hit_bucket. also add a panel that shows kernel_choice distribution by seq_len and kv_hit.

elaine: agree. also need token-level waterfall breakdown per-request: queue_wait | kernel_launch | kernel_exec | memcpy | postproc. we have coarse timers now but not per-token waterfall.

oliver: for dashboards I suggest these panels: 
- batch_size_histogram (stacked by route, time window 5m)
- queue_wait_p50_p95_p99 per route
- token_latency_waterfall: avg/median/99 for each stage (labels as above)
- kernel_choice_heatmap: kernel vs seq_len_bucket vs kv_hit_bucket
- kv_cache_hit_ratio timeseries with annotations when kernel_choice switches

sara: and add alerts: 
- alert when p99 token latency increases >15% vs 1h baseline AND kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.5
- alert when packed_matmul_v2 kernel_usage for seq_len<=32 > 10% of requests on a route

perf-bot: Automated note: added metric 'redwood_runtime_kernel_choice_total{kernel,route,model,seq_len_bucket,kv_hit_bucket}' to exposition list. scrape interval: 15s.

mike: thanks bot. timeline for dashboards/alerts?

raj: I can wire metrics into grafana panels by EOD tomorrow if perf-bot metric lands in prod. will also add an exploration dashboard to correlate traces.

elaine: can we also tag traces with 'kernel_variant' so trace UI can filter by kernel? that will speed triage.

sara: yes — I'll add kernel_variant to the trace spans and include the selector decision id.

oliver: longer-term change: change selector to use cost model that estimates memcpy overhead when kv_cache_hit_ratio > threshold and favors the kernel with lower estimated tail cost for tiny remaining token workloads. we should also experiment with microbatch packing that respects seq_len boundaries.

mike: plan sounds good. action items: 
1) perf-bot metric in prod (done)
2) sara adds kernel_variant to traces (in PR)
3) raj builds grafana panels and alerts (ETA: 24h)
4) oliver and sara prototype selector cost-model (follow-up next week)

sara: I'll open the PR for trace tags now and add a small canary to prevent selector flip for seq_len<=32 until cost-model lands.

mike: :thumbsup: keep updates here. if anyone sees staging spike, tag @sara and @raj.

perf-bot: Deploy note: selector canary config rolled to staging at 1951234590 by sara.

sara: test run after canary shows p99 back to baseline for /chat/light (within 3%). will monitor for 1 hour. :relieved:

oliver: great. postmortem-ish: we need smaller unit tests for selector heuristics that simulate high KV-hit short seq scenarios. filing a ticket now.

mike: thanks all. good triage and instrumentation plan. :rocket:
